task.pr_title: Make equirectangular reflections / refractions backwards compatible.

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
This change is problematic since `WebGLObjects.update()` should only be called for instance of `Mesh`, `Points`, `Line` and `Sprite`. So objects that have a geometry.

Right now, it's called for all 3D objects in a scene.

evidence.thread_resolution:
Mugen87: How about completely removing the changes related to `WebGLRenderer.compile()`. It seems they do not belong to this PR.
mrdoob: Unfortunately it does belong to this PR, and that took me ~4h to figure out. Let me try to summarize...

Basically, when we call `new WebGLCubeRenderTarget().fromEquirectangularTexture()` within a render, we're doing a nested render() which changes the state of the parent render() and we end up with a black render.

So I tried to change `fromEquirectangularTexture()` to be more like `WebGLShadowMap` which doesn't call `render()` but `renderBufferDirect()`. `renderBufferDirect()` depends on geometry attributes having been uploaded in order to work, and that's what happens in `objects.update( object )`.

Until I added this line I was just getting a black screen with no warnings anywhere (debugging WebGL is fun!).

Anyway, I didn't know if this was the right thing to do. Now I have to check what's the render flow when we render mirrors and see what approach to go with.
Mugen87: Okay, this dependency is indeed not obvious^^.

Well, if there is no other solution you could still do:

```js
if ( object.geometry ) objects.update( object );
```
in order to fix `webgl_materials_compile`.
mrdoob: Ah! Interesting. I'll give it a try tomorrow 🙏
mrdoob: Done! 🤞
Mugen87: Only one broken example left! Getting there 👍
